images.caption:
A "Larkin Toad" eyeing up Hull's History Centre building where all Larkin's manuscripts and papers have been catalogued and stored, its an impressive building and seems to be a collaberation between Hull City Council Library Local Studies Department and Hull University.
TOADS REVISITED
Walking around in the park
Should feel better than work:
The lake, the sunshine,
The grass to lie on,
Blurred playground noises
Beyond black-stockinged nurses -
Not a bad place to be.
Yet it doesn't suit me.
Being one of the men
You meet of an afternoon:
Palsied old step-takers,
Hare-eyed clerks with the jitters,
Waxed-fleshed out-patients
Still vague from accidents,
And characters in long coats
Deep in the litter-baskets -
All dodging the toad work
By being stupid or weak.
Think of being them!
Hearing the hours chime,
Watching the bread delivered,
The sun by clouds covered,
The children going home;
Think of being them,
Turning over their failures
By some bed of lobelias,
Nowhere to go but indoors,
Nor friends but empty chairs -
No, give me my in-tray,
My loaf-haired secretary,
My shall-I-keep-the-call-in-Sir:
What else can I answer,
When the lights come on at four
At the end of another year?
Give me your arm, old toad;
Help me down Cemetery road.

Philip Larkin 122-1985.

images.filename: Michael and Christine Egan Memorials, Kingston upon Hull Dec23.jpg
images.caption: Two small memorials to the Hull-born Michael and Christine Egan at their new permanent site by the Hull History Centre in Kingston upon Hull, having originally been located in Queen's Gardens' Peace Garden. The two siblings, the latter of which had a distinguished career in northern Canada as a nurse for First Nations communities, were killed upon the collapse of the South Tower of the World Trade Center in the September 11th, 2001 attacks. Michael was working on the 104th floor for the Aon Corporation, and Christine had come to visit that morning. An Inuktitut epitaph on Christine's memorial reads "Qatangutiga Naligimaliktara" - "Dearly Beloved".

images.filename: Ferens Art Gallery at Night - geograph.org.uk - 1560622.jpg
images.caption: Ferens Art Gallery at Night Ferens Art Gallery is situated in Victoria square in Hull.  The area is illuminated by high pressure sodium lighting which gives rise to this weird effect.  Superficially, it looks as though the square was deserted, but the long exposure has 'lost' the people as none were standing still at the time!

images.caption: Fountain in Princes Quay Princes Quay is a shopping complex in the centre of Hull and is built on 'stilts' above the former Princes Dock.  There are two fountains in the dock now and this is the most northerly one.  The shopping centre itself can be seen in the background.  The photograph was taken with an exposure time of about six seconds to give this effect.
